This scheme distributes the 8 voxels of any interpolation cell across all 8 available memory modules [S2].

The evidence explicitly states that the memory organization technique distributes voxels across 8 memory modules. It further clarifies that this allows fetching any tri-linear cell (which consists of 8 adjacent voxels) in one memory access, implying that the 8 voxels of the cell are distributed across the 8 available modules. The formulas provided confirm that the memory module index $k$ is determined by the parity of the coordinates, ensuring that adjacent voxels in a tri-linear cell map to different modules.
supported
This organization is identical to that used in the VIRIM geometry unit and SGI Reality Engine [S2].

The evidence explicitly states in the 'System Architecture' section of Source [S2] that the volume data in VIRIM is stored in an '8-way interleaved memory system, identical in organization to the 3D texture memory discussed in Section 3.' Section 3 of Source [S2] describes the memory organization used in the SGI Reality Engine. Therefore, the claim that the organization is identical to that used in the VIRIM geometry unit and SGI Reality Engine is directly supported by the text.

Arithmetic is still performed in 32-bit floating point, with results truncated upon writing to the texture [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that arithmetic is performed in 32-bit floating point and results are truncated upon writing to the texture. The evidence explicitly states: 'Note that arithmetic operations are still performed in 32-bit floating point, meaning that results are periodically truncated as they are written to the destination textures.' This directly supports every part of the claim.

This yields roughly twice the performance (half the penalty) compared to 32-bit textures, with little visually discernible degradation [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that using 16-bit textures yields roughly twice the performance (half the penalty) compared to 32-bit textures, with little visually discernible degradation. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'using 32-bit floating-point textures to store quantities yields roughly half the performance of 16-bit textures' (which is equivalent to 16-bit textures yielding twice the performance of 32-bit) and 'Surprisingly, there is little visually discernible degradation that results from using 16-bit storage'. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
supported
A memory organization technique where voxels are distributed across 8 memory modules based on coordinate parity [S2].

The claim states that voxels are distributed across 8 memory modules based on coordinate parity. The evidence explicitly defines the memory module index $k$ using the formula $k = (x mod 2) + 2 (y mod 2) + 4 (z mod 2)$, which relies on the parity (modulo 2) of the coordinates. It also confirms there are 8 memory modules and that this technique allows fetching tri-linear cells (which consist of 8 adjacent voxels) in one access.
supported
This allows the texture engine to fetch any tri-linear cell in a single memory access without bank conflicts [S2].

The claim states that the texture engine can fetch any tri-linear cell in a single memory access without bank conflicts. The evidence in Source [S2] explicitly states: 'Eight-way memory interleaving allows the texture engine to fetch any tri-linear cell in one memory access.' It further explains that this is achieved by distributing voxels across 8 memory modules based on the parity of their coordinates (x, y, z), ensuring that the 8 voxels required for a tri-linear cell are distributed across different modules, thus avoiding conflicts and allowing a single access.
supported

For hardware architectures that support multi-bank or multi-module memory systems (such as the SGI Reality Engine or the VIRIM geometry unit), a different organization is used to guarantee that no two voxels in a $2 \times 2 \times 2$ cell map to the same memory module [S2].

The evidence explicitly states that the SGI Reality Engine uses eight-way interleaved texture memory to fetch any tri-linear cell (a 2x2x2 cell of eight adjacent voxels) in one memory access. It provides the specific formula for calculating the memory module index based on the parity of the voxel coordinates, which ensures that the 8 voxels in a 2x2x2 cell map to 8 distinct memory modules (0-7). Furthermore, the evidence confirms that the VIRIM geometry unit uses an 8-way interleaved memory system identical in organization to this scheme. Therefore, the claim that these architectures use a specific organization to guarantee no two voxels in a 2x2x2 cell map to the same module is fully supported by the text.

It distinguishes between standard row-major storage, which relies on hardware caching for spatial coherence [G], and hardware-specific interleaving schemes designed to ensure that all voxels required for a single tri-linear interpolation fetch reside in distinct memory modules, allowing the entire cell to be retrieved in a single memory transaction [S2].

The evidence supports the claim regarding 'hardware-specific interleaving schemes' and the specific mechanism of distributing voxels across 8 memory modules to allow fetching a tri-linear cell in a single memory transaction (as detailed in Source [S2]). However, the evidence does not contain any information or comparison regarding 'standard row-major storage' or its reliance on 'hardware caching for spatial coherence'. Therefore, only part of the claim is supported by the provided text.
supported
Here, $k$ is a 3-bit index (0–7) determining the memory module, derived from the parity of the voxel coordinates [S2].

The claim states that $k$ is a 3-bit index (0–7) determining the memory module, derived from the parity of the voxel coordinates. The evidence explicitly states: 'The number of memory modules is 8, determined by the 3-bit index $k$ derived from the parity of the voxel coordinates.' It also provides the formula $k = (x mod 2) + 2 (y mod 2) + 4 (z mod 2)$, which confirms that $k$ is calculated based on the parity (mod 2) of the coordinates x, y, and z, resulting in a value between 0 and 7 (3 bits).
supported
For a voxel with address $a = [zyx]$, the memory module index $k$ and the local index $i$ within that module are calculated as [S2]:

The claim states that for a voxel with address $a = [zyx]$, the memory module index $k$ and local index $i$ are calculated using specific formulas. Source [S2] explicitly provides these exact formulas: $k = (x mod 2) + 2 (y mod 2) + 4 (z mod 2)$ and $i = floor(x/2) + 2 floor(y/2) + 4 floor(z/2)$. The source confirms that this organization is used to distribute voxels across 8 memory modules. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present and supported by the evidence.
supported
The local index $i$ determines the position within the module [S2].

The source text explicitly states that a voxel with address a = [zyx] is stored in memory module k at index i, and provides the formula for calculating i. This confirms that the local index i determines the position (index) within the memory module.

Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

The concept of 8-way interleaved texture memory originated in high-performance 3D graphics engines such as the SGI Reality Engine [S2].

The claim states that the concept of 8-way interleaved texture memory originated in high-performance 3D graphics engines such as the SGI Reality Engine. The provided evidence explicitly states in Source [S2] passages that 'high performance 3D graphics engines, such as the SGI Reality Engine [Ake93], use eight-way interleaved texture memory.' Furthermore, the evidence links this specific memory organization (defined by the parity-based indexing formula) to the SGI Reality Engine and notes that the VIRIM geometry unit's memory system is 'identical in organization' to the 3D texture memory discussed (which is attributed to the SGI context). Thus, the evidence supports the assertion that this concept is associated with and used in such engines.
supported
This architecture was notably used in the VIRIM (Volume Rendering Image Machine) system, which employed a dedicated 8-way interleaved memory system for its geometry unit [S2].

The evidence explicitly states in the 'System Architecture' section of Source [S2] that 'The volume data is stored in a dedicated 8-way interleaved memory system, identical in organization to the 3D texture memory discussed in Section 3.' Additionally, the notes confirm that this organization is identical to the system used in the VIRIM geometry unit. The claim accurately reflects these facts.
